faults.figma_prompt: Modern Japanese TV anime: crisp clean line art, cel shading with two-tone shadows, vivid saturated colour, painted skies with light rays. Scene: a long paved park path under lush tropical trees in the Philippines at morning, high angle, the family small in the frame and seen from behind, walking away: a Filipino man in his forties with a black topknot with a few grey strands, a long dark grey coat, a red handkerchief on his wrist, hand in hand with a young Filipina woman with long black hair in a simple long dark blue dress; beside her their son, a small Filipino boy of about six with black hair, a beige t-shirt, green shorts and dark sneakers, arms at his sides; beside the boy trots a slim black short-haired Philippine street dog with a white chest patch, one ear folded down and one upright, a red kerchief tied around his neck, his head turned a little to the side so both ears show. Exactly three people and one dog, nobody else. Single image, no panels, no border, the picture fills the whole vertical frame. Vertical 9:16. No text, no logos, no watermarks.
faults.fix_note: Four full-quality redraws tried and thrown away (melted joined hands; both ears folded and a white spot on the rump; dog walking the wrong way; Indio drawn as a stern old man). The old still is restored.

usman_note: Two dogs, two answers. (1) Pugad Lawin, k07 and k11: this dog IS Usman. Episode 49 ends with Usman at Indio's feet 'in the present now, no longer vanishing', episode 50 opens years later with the same three marks (black, white chest, one folded ear) beside Indio's child, and the fact check of this very script lists 'kami ni Usman' among the invented things in the episode, so Usman is on screen. The series cast says he always wears the red kerchief; the prompts left it out. The missing kerchief is therefore an off_model fault on k07 (already inside reader 1's must-fix entry) and on k11 (added). (2) The first meadow, k24, k25, k27, k28: not a fault. The narrator calls it only 'a black dog' in another world at the very beginning, before Indio or anyone could have tied a kerchief on him; the scene works because the three body marks alone tell the viewer who he is, and a kerchief there would contradict 'the very beginning'. Those keys are judged only on the body marks (one folded ear, short coat, chest patch), which is where k24, k25 and k28 fail.
